/-!
# Conjecture 1.86

by A. L. Shmel'kin

Is it true that the identical relations of a polycyclic group have a finite basis?

An identical relation (law) of a group $G$ is a word $w$ in the free group $F_\infty$ of
countable rank such that $w(g_1, g_2, \dots) = 1$ for all $g_1, g_2, \dots \in G$. The laws of
$G$ form a fully invariant subgroup of $F_\infty$. A set $S$ of laws is a *basis* for the laws
of $G$ if every law of $G$ is a consequence of $S$, i.e. lies in the verbal subgroup of
$F_\infty$ determined by $S$ (the fully invariant closure of $S$). Equivalently, the variety of
groups generated by $G$ is finitely based.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
def IsPolycyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (H : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G),
    Monotone H ∧ H 0 = ⊥ ∧ H (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, ∃ _ : ((H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ)).Normal,
      IsCyclic (H i.succ ⧸ (H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ))
blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is *polycyclic* if it has a subnormal series
$1 = H_0 \trianglelefteq H_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq H_n = G$, i.e. a chain of
subgroups with each $H_i$ normal in $H_{i+1}$, all of whose factors $H_{i+1}/H_i$ are cyclic.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `IsSolvable` (derived series, but allows non-finitely-generated abelian factors), `Group.IsNilpotent`, `CompositionSeries` (requires maximal/simple steps, not cyclic factors).
justification.name: Kourovka.«1.86».IsPolycyclic
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of polycyclic group (no hits for 'polycyclic' in Mathlib, FormalConjecturesForMathlib, or FormalConjectures).

blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ is *polycyclic* if it has a subnormal series
$1 = H_0 \trianglelefteq H_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq H_n = G$, i.e. a chain of
subgroups with each $H_i$ normal in $H_{i+1}$, all of whose factors $H_{i+1}/H_i$ are cyclic. -/
def IsPolycyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (H : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G),
    Monotone H ∧ H 0 = ⊥ ∧ H (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, ∃ _ : ((H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ)).Normal,
      IsCyclic (H i.succ ⧸ (H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ))

def laws (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ) :=
  ⨅ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, φ.ker
blocks.docstring:
The subgroup of identical relations (laws) of the group $G$: the words $w$ in the free group
$F_\infty$ of countable rank such that $\varphi(w) = 1$ for every homomorphism
$\varphi \colon F_\infty \to G$, i.e. $w(g_1, g_2, \dots) = 1$ for all $g_1, g_2, \dots \in G$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `MonoidHom.ker`, `FreeGroup.lift`; Mathlib's `Submodule.IsFullyInvariant` is for modules only, and there is no group-variety machinery.
justification.name: Kourovka.«1.86».laws

/-- The subgroup of identical relations (laws) of the group $G$: the words $w$ in the free group
$F_\infty$ of countable rank such that $\varphi(w) = 1$ for every homomorphism

blocks.code:
def verbalClosure (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ) :=
  Subgroup.closure {w | ∃ s ∈ S, ∃ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* FreeGroup ℕ, φ s = w}
blocks.docstring:
The verbal subgroup of $F_\infty$ determined by a set $S$ of words: the subgroup generated
by all values of the words in $S$ on elements of $F_\infty$, i.e. by all images of elements of
$S$ under endomorphisms of $F_\infty$. This is the fully invariant closure of $S$, and its
elements are exactly the consequences of the identical relations in $S$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Subgroup.closure`, `Subgroup.normalClosure` (only closes under conjugation, not under all endomorphisms, so it does not capture consequences of laws).
justification.name: Kourovka.«1.86».verbalClosure
justification.why_needed: No Mathlib definition of verbal subgroups or fully invariant closure in a free group; defined as `Subgroup.closure` of all endomorphic images of the given words.

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_laws_iff {w : FreeGroup ℕ} :
    w ∈ laws G ↔ ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1 := by
  simp only [laws, Subgroup.mem_iInf, MonoidHom.mem_ker]
  refine ⟨fun h f => h _, fun h φ => ?_⟩
  rw [FreeGroup.lift_unique φ (fun _ => rfl)]
  exact h _
blocks.docstring:
A word $w$ is a law of $G$ if and only if it evaluates to $1$ under every substitution of
elements of $G$ for its variables.

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem map_laws_le (φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* FreeGroup ℕ) : (laws G).map φ ≤ laws G := by
  rintro w ⟨v, hv, rfl⟩
  simp only [laws, Subgroup.mem_iInf, MonoidHom.mem_ker, SetLike.mem_coe] at hv ⊢
  exact fun ψ => hv (ψ.comp φ)

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem verbalClosure_le_laws_iff {S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)} :
    verbalClosure S ≤ laws G ↔ S ⊆ laws G := by
  constructor
  · intro h s hs
    exact h (Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨s, hs, MonoidHom.id _, rfl⟩)
  · intro h
    apply Subgroup.closure_le _ |>.2
    rintro w ⟨s, hs, φ, rfl⟩
    exact map_laws_le φ ⟨s, h hs, rfl⟩

claims.decomposer_note: Implicit universal quantifier over all polycyclic groups G (groups with a subnormal series with cyclic factors); 'finite basis' means the set of laws (identities) of G — a fully invariant subgroup of the free group of countable rank — is the fully invariant (verbal) closure of finitely many words, i.e. the variety var(G) is finitely based; this is a yes/no question, so the Prop is the universal assertion with answer(sorry) ↔.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful proposition: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ polycyclic G : Type, ∃ finite S ⊆ FreeGroup ℕ with fully-invariant (verbal) closure of S = laws of G. Their bespoke definitions are mutually equivalent and match the standard ones (subnormal series with cyclic factors; laws = words killed by every homomorphism F_∞ → G / every substitution; verbal closure = subgroup generated by all endomorphic images, or equivalently the sInf of fully invariant subgroups containing S, or c08's semantic 'every group satisfying S satisfies the laws of G' — equivalent by Neumann's theory since fully invariant = verbal in F_∞ and F_∞/V(S) is relatively free). I verified with pp.explicit that in the IsCyclic-of-quotient encodings the quotient's group structure is built from the existential Normal witness. c06 was chosen for its clear docstrings, self-contained theorem statement, and short fully-proved API/test lemmas (mem_laws_iff, full invariance of laws, basis consists of laws, trivial/cyclic groups polycyclic) as CONTRIBUTING.md asks for bespoke definitions. Compiles with only the sorry warning.

/-!

by A. L. Shmel'kin

namespace Kourovka.«1.86»

/-- A group $G$ is *polycyclic* if it has a subnormal series
$1 = H_0 \trianglelefteq H_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq H_n = G$, i.e. a chain of
subgroups with each $H_i$ normal in $H_{i+1}$, all of whose factors $H_{i+1}/H_i$ are cyclic. -/
def IsPolycyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (H : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G),
    Monotone H ∧ H 0 = ⊥ ∧ H (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, ∃ _ : ((H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ)).Normal,
      IsCyclic (H i.succ ⧸ (H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ))

/-- The subgroup of identical relations (laws) of the group $G$: the words $w$ in the free group
$F_\infty$ of countable rank such that $\varphi(w) = 1$ for every homomorphism
$\varphi \colon F_\infty \to G$, i.e. $w(g_1, g_2, \dots) = 1$ for all $g_1, g_2, \dots \in G$. -/
def laws (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ) :=
  ⨅ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, φ.ker

/-- The verbal subgroup of $F_\infty$ determined by a set $S$ of words: the subgroup generated
by all values of the words in $S$ on elements of $F_\infty$, i.e. by all images of elements of
$S$ under endomorphisms of $F_\infty$. This is the fully invariant closure of $S$, and its
elements are exactly the consequences of the identical relations in $S$. -/
def verbalClosure (S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Subgroup (FreeGroup ℕ) :=
  Subgroup.closure {w | ∃ s ∈ S, ∃ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* FreeGroup ℕ, φ s = w}

/--
Is it true that the identical relations of a polycyclic group have a finite basis?

That is, for every polycyclic group $G$, is there a finite set $S$ of words whose consequences
(the verbal subgroup of $F_\infty$ determined by $S$) are exactly the identical relations of $G$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«1.86» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPolycyclic G →
      ∃ S : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ), verbalClosure ↑S = laws G := by
  sorry

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A word $w$ is a law of $G$ if and only if it evaluates to $1$ under every substitution of
elements of $G$ for its variables. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_laws_iff {w : FreeGroup ℕ} :
    w ∈ laws G ↔ ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1 := by
  simp only [laws, Subgroup.mem_iInf, MonoidHom.mem_ker]
  refine ⟨fun h f => h _, fun h φ => ?_⟩
  rw [FreeGroup.lift_unique φ (fun _ => rfl)]
  exact h _

/-- The laws of $G$ form a fully invariant subgroup of $F_\infty$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem map_laws_le (φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* FreeGroup ℕ) : (laws G).map φ ≤ laws G := by
  rintro w ⟨v, hv, rfl⟩
  simp only [laws, Subgroup.mem_iInf, MonoidHom.mem_ker, SetLike.mem_coe] at hv ⊢
  exact fun ψ => hv (ψ.comp φ)

/-- The consequences of a set $S$ of words are laws of $G$ if and only if the words in $S$ are
laws of $G$. In particular a basis for the laws of $G$ consists of laws of $G$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem verbalClosure_le_laws_iff {S : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)} :
    verbalClosure S ≤ laws G ↔ S ⊆ laws G := by
  constructor
  · intro h s hs
    exact h (Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨s, hs, MonoidHom.id _, rfl⟩)
  · intro h
    apply Subgroup.closure_le _ |>.2
    rintro w ⟨s, hs, φ, rfl⟩
    exact map_laws_le φ ⟨s, h hs, rfl⟩

/-- The trivial group is polycyclic. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPolycyclic_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton G] : IsPolycyclic G :=
  ⟨0, fun _ => ⊥, monotone_const, rfl, Subsingleton.elim _ _, fun i => i.elim0⟩

/-- Cyclic groups are polycyclic. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsCyclic.isPolycyclic [IsCyclic G] : IsPolycyclic G := by
  refine ⟨1, ![⊥, ⊤], ?_, rfl, rfl, ?_⟩
  · exact Fin.monotone_iff_le_succ.2 fun i => by fin_cases i; simp
  · intro i
    fin_cases i
    refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    · simp only [Fin.zero_eta, Fin.castSucc_zero, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Fin.succ_zero_eq_one,
        Matrix.cons_val_one, Subgroup.bot_subgroupOf]
      infer_instance
    · simp only [Fin.zero_eta, Fin.castSucc_zero, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Fin.succ_zero_eq_one,
        Matrix.cons_val_one]
      exact isCyclic_of_surjective (QuotientGroup.mk' _) (QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective _)

end Kourovka.«1.86»

items: Polycyclic is defined directly as in the decomposition notes: existence of a finite chain `⊥ = H 0 ≤ … ≤ H (Fin.last n) = ⊤` of subgroups (encoded as `Monotone H` on `Fin (n+1)`) with each `H i` normal in `H (i+1)` (via `(H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ)` being `Normal`) and each factor `H i.succ ⧸ (H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ)` cyclic. The `Normal` witness is an anonymous existential binder, and `#print` with `pp.explicit` confirmed that `IsCyclic` on the quotient uses the group structure induced by that witness. The equivalent characterization 'solvable with all subgroups finitely generated' (Hirsch) was not used, to stay closest to the standard definition.

'Consequence of a set of laws' is taken syntactically: the verbal (fully invariant) closure in `FreeGroup ℕ`, defined as `Subgroup.closure` of all images of elements of `S` under endomorphisms of `FreeGroup ℕ`. This equals the smallest fully invariant subgroup containing `S`, and by the standard theory (H. Neumann, Varieties of Groups) it coincides with the set of words holding in every group satisfying `S`; the semantic formulation (quantifying over all groups satisfying `S`) was not used.
Words live in the free group of countable rank `FreeGroup ℕ`, the standard `F_∞` for laws; a finite basis involves finitely many variables in any case.
The universal quantifier over polycyclic groups uses `G : Type` (universe 0), following the other Kourovka files; this loses nothing because polycyclic groups are finitely generated, hence countable.

`answer(True)` asserts that every polycyclic group has finitely based laws; `answer(False)` asserts some polycyclic group does not. The trivial group (n = 0 series) is polycyclic and trivially finitely based, so the degenerate case behaves correctly.
Five short auxiliary declarations were added (three `category API`, two `category test`) with complete proofs to exercise the bespoke definitions, as CONTRIBUTING.md requests for bespoke definitions.

reviewer_notes: Modeling choices (shared by all candidates and adopted): (1) the implicit universal quantifier over all polycyclic groups, with G : Type (no loss since polycyclic groups are finitely generated hence countable); (2) 'finite basis' taken syntactically as V(G) = fully invariant closure of a finite set of words in FreeGroup ℕ, which is the standard definition and equivalent to the semantic 'var(G) finitely based'; (3) polycyclic via a subnormal series ⊥ = H₀ ⊴ … ⊴ Hₙ = ⊤ with cyclic factors (n = 0 gives exactly the trivial group, which is polycyclic and trivially finitely based, so the degenerate case is harmless). answer(True) asserts every polycyclic group has finitely based laws, answer(False) that some polycyclic group does not. No candidate omitted the slot; there were no faithfulness defects in any candidate, so the choice among them was stylistic. Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib have no notion of polycyclic group, group law, or verbal subgroup; a maintainer may wish to move IsPolycyclic/laws/verbalClosure to FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
